newsitem.title: BELARUS: Police clash with Belarus demonstrators.
newsitem.headline: Police clash with Belarus demonstrators.

text.p: Belarus police and OMON special forces clashed with several hundred demonstrators in the capital Minsk on Sunday during a march protesting against President Alexander Lukashenko's referendum to increase his powers.

Reuter correspondent Yuri Svirko said several hundred protesters had broken away from the main group of demonstrators and forced their way through police lines, heading towards the parliament. Some officers used their truncheons in an unsuccessful effort to prevent the demonstrators moving on.
Some demonstrators were knocked to the ground but there appeared to be no serious injuries.
The demonstration, called a "March of Silence", had started in the morning, and between 5,000 and 10,000 people moved slowly from the outskirts of Minsk towards the centre.

But police and special forces barred the protesters from entering the main Skoriny Prospekt. They surrounded one large group, banging their riot shields with truncheons. Police reinforcements waited in buses and trucks near the scene of the confrontation.
The march was the latest in a series of protests against Lukashenko's proposals, which would allow him to extend his term in office by two years without new elections.
